description.short_caption: Histopathology of skin biopsy showing fungal elements with surrounding inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a high-power view of a skin biopsy stained with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain. Numerous round to oval fungal elements are visible, highlighted in magenta, consistent with fungal hyphae or yeast forms. The surrounding tissue shows inflammatory infiltrates and some degree of cellular disruption. The magenta staining indicates the presence of polysaccharides in fungal cell walls.
visible_findings: round to oval fungal elements stained magenta
periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain highlighting fungal cell walls

description.short_caption: Facial skin lesion with central ulceration and crusting.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up view of the skin on the face, focusing on a lesion below the eye. The lesion has a central area of ulceration with surrounding erythema and crusting. There are additional smaller lesions nearby, including a small papule with a dark center. The skin appears slightly erythematous in the surrounding area.

description.short_caption: Axial MRI of the brain showing abnormal hyperintensities.
description.detailed_description: This axial MRI image of the brain demonstrates hyperintense lesions in the periventricular white matter, visible on a T2-weighted or FLAIR sequence. The ventricles appear normal in size and shape. The hyperintensities are suggestive of an inflammatory, infectious, or demyelinating process.
visible_findings: hyperintense lesions in periventricular white matter

description.short_caption: Ulcerative lesion with eschar and surrounding erythema on the forearm.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a forearm with a central ulcerative lesion covered by a dark eschar. Surrounding the lesion is an area of erythema and scattered smaller erythematous papules. The skin appears inflamed, and the lesion is suggestive of a necrotic process. The image is well-lit, and the lesion is clearly visible.
